The schools teach in Japanese now.
The words written on Yun's pages are in the King's letters, like the keeper's note.
King Sejong made his letters for the people's own language.
lines.junior:
In 1938, Korean became only a choice subject in the schools.
Now the schools teach in Japanese.
The words on Yun's pages are written in the King's letters, just like the keeper's note.
King Sejong made his letters for the people's own language.
lines.master:
In 1938, Korean was reduced to only a choice subject in the schools.
The schools now teach in Japanese.
The words on Yun's pages are written in the King's letters, exactly like the keeper's note.
King Sejong created his letters for the people's own language.
